subject: Pricing tilt & seamless switch proposal
messages:
From: Oliver Chang <oliver@cloudworks.io>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 8 Dec 2025 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Evaluating a replacement — pricing & migration asks

Hi Jonas,

Thanks for taking the quick intro last week. We finished an internal sweep of our current inference spend and are exploring a swap away from our current vendor to reduce per-token cost and improve tail latency on long context jobs. Before committing to a pilot we'd like to understand the practical economics and upgrade path. High-level asks: 

- Can Redwood match or beat our current blended per-token effective price for the next 12 months? We can share usage slices (burst vs steady-state).
- What migration credits or onboarding incentives do you offer for a 3-year committed relationship?
- Will there be a seamless model compatibility guarantee for our existing prompts (we rely heavily on KV cache patterns)?
- Any constraints on burst/Dedicated capacity for inference during our migration window?

Attaching a short CSV of our monthly consumption profile (summary attached). We also have an internal security checklist — Priya (cc'd) will share it soon.

Can you put together a slim offer (pricing, credits, ramp timeline) that I can circulate to our procurement team this week? If helpful, propose a 30–45 minute slot for a quick walkthrough.

Appreciate it —
Oliver
Oliver Chang
Head of Platform Engineering, CloudWorks
oliver@cloudworks.io

Attachments: cloudworks-usage-summary.csv (CSV stub)
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Oliver Chang <oliver@cloudworks.io>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 8 Dec 2025 12:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Evaluating a replacement — pricing & migration asks

Hi Oliver —

Thanks — got the usage summary. We can pull together a concise offer and a recommended migration plan that minimizes downtime and preserves prompt fidelity. High level first pass (will follow up with numbers + attachments):

- Pricing tilt: a blended per-token parity offer for the first 12 months with an option to convert to volume-tier pricing thereafter.
- Migration credits: up to 3 months of committed-credit applied to cover engineering time and burst capacity for the cutover (amount depends on committed ARR).
- Compatibility: we run a pre-flight prompt compatibility pass and KV-preservation validation as part of the pilot; will surface any prompt drop-offs ahead of rollout.
- Capacity: offer includes dedicated burst capacity reservation for a 2-week cutover window with guaranteed throughput.

I attached an initial econ sketch to illustrate the components (see initial-econ-sketch.pdf). Jordan — can you review the credit and capacity buckets and flag anything risky with the runbook?

If that looks reasonable, Oliver — how about Wed 10th at 10am PT for a 30 minute walkthrough?

Best,
Jonas Weber

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 9 Dec 2025 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Internal — CloudWorks concession options and recommended offer

Team,

Recap: CloudWorks is willing to move if we can (a) hit blended per-token parity for the first 12 months, (b) provide migration credits to offset cutover burst costs, and (c) guarantee compatibility for their KV-heavy prompt set. They looped Priya from security — we'll need to be ready with SOC2 evidence and network diagrams.

I sketched three discrete concession packages in pricing-options-VM1.xlsx (attached) — summary below:

Option A — Light: parity for 12mo + 1 month credit (small onboarding credit). No dedicated burst included.
Pros: minimal revenue impact; Cons: higher operational risk for cutover; might not win.

Option B — Preferred: 10% below parity for 12mo + 2 months migration credit + 2-week dedicated burst reservation + canonical migration runbook and evaluation window.
Pros: higher win probability; preserves unit economics via conversion to tiered pricing after year 1.
Cons: upfront credits impact.

Option C — Aggressive: 15% below parity for 18mo + 3 months credit + extended success engineering support and 4-week reserved capacity.
Pros: highest likelihood to displace incumbent; Cons: highest short-term hit.

Notes & asks:
- Jordan: confirm cost of the 2-week burst reservation and whether the engineering time estimate is realistic (I used 80 hours SRE/SE).
- Marissa: are you comfortable with the ask tied to an annualized commitment of 3 years (they favor longer term if price is right)?
- Also need approval to share SOC2 artifact links and to open a DocuSign for a pilot commitment.

I'll hold off externalizing until I have signoff on a single preferred package (I recommend Option B as a balance).

Thanks —
Jonas

Attachments: pricing-options-VM1.xlsx (Excel stub)

Subject: Offer: Seamless switch package — CloudWorks (CW-4821)

Oliver —

Appreciate the conversation this week. Based on your usage slices and internal alignment, attached is our proposed Seamless Switch package (summary below). This is intentionally compact so you can circulate it to procurement: 

Offer summary (Preferred — Option B):
- Pricing: 10% below your current blended per-token effective price for the first 12 months (detailed tier schedule in attached PDF).
- Migration credits: 2 months of committed-credit applied as usage credits to cover burst/engineering during cutover (applies to the first billing cycle after go-live).
- Capacity: 2-week reserved burst pool (pre-booked GPUs) during cutover window, includes runbook support for hot-warm migrations.
- Compatibility: pre-flight prompt verification and KV-cache validation; we'll run a compatibility sweep on a representative prompt set during the pilot.
- Commit: 3-year term with annualized billing. Early-termination terms documented in the attached.

What we need from you to proceed:
1) Confirmation of commitment window (3 years) and primary start date for the pilot cutover window.
2) Signed pilot addendum (DocuSign link below) — includes the migration credit schedule and reserved capacity booking clause.
3) Security checklist answers from Priya so we can share SOC2 artifacts and the network diagram.

Attachments: redwood-seamless-switch-offer-v1.pdf (PDF stub)
Related links: DocuSign pilot addendum (https://www.docusign.com/fake-link/CW-4821), HubSpot deal (https://hubspot.example.com/deal/CW-4821)

Next steps: if acceptable, we can schedule the pilot kickoff the week after sign-off and lock the reserved burst dates. Happy to discuss details on Fri 12/12 at 9am PT — would that work?

Best regards,
